# Hobbies, Sports & Kids — category guidance (auto-generated from live market data, 2026-08-26)

## Price sanity (NPR, live market data)
- Other Hobby, Sport & Kids items: typically around 700, most listings 150–3,000 (54 listings)
- Children's Items: typically around 450, most listings 50–3,000 (32 listings)
- Sports: typically around 3,700, most listings 750–7,000 (14 listings)
- Musical Instruments: typically around 4,500, most listings 700–15,500 (8 listings)
- Fitness & Gym: typically around 2,500, most listings 500–5,700 (7 listings)
- Music, Books & Movies: typically around 5,000, most listings 1,000–15,500 (7 listings)

This is mostly a low-value category, so cheap prices are normal, not suspicious. The scam-price
check matters mainly for the pricier goods here (guitars/keyboards, gym machines, branded sports
gear): a near-new branded instrument or machine priced far below its known market value -> hold.
Musical Instruments, Fitness & Gym, and Music/Books/Movies have thin data (n < 10) — treat those
ranges as rough and lean on general judgment. Collectibles (trading cards, signed memorabilia)
legitimately price far outside all ranges, from NPR 20 cards to six-figure signed items; do not
flag them on price alone.

## What good listings look like
- "Official Nepal Cricket Team Signed Bat (2023 ACC Premier Cup)"
- "♟️ MAGNETIC FOLDING CHESS SET ♟️ अब चेसका गोटी कहिल्यै नखस्ने, नहराउने टेन्सन सकियो!"
- "🔥 SUPERHERO ACTION FIGURE – बच्चाहरूको रमाइलो खेलौनाको शानदार सेट 🔥"
- "🇳🇵 Nepal Cricket Jersey | Dashain Offer 🔥 Rs.659 Only | Premium Quality | Limited Stock"
- "Mithila Paintings"

A good listing names the item type plus a distinguishing attribute (brand, team/edition, set
contents, material). Mixed Nepali/English titles, emoji, and promo phrasing are normal here and
are not spam signals by themselves.

## Category-specific hold signals
- Duplicate reposting: the same product posted multiple times by one seller is the one recorded
  editor rejection in this category -> hold repeats of an already-live listing.
- High-priced memorabilia (signed bats, autographs, rare cards) that claims authenticity but gives
  zero provenance detail (no event, year, or certificate mentioned) -> hold; with concrete
  provenance in the text (e.g. named tournament and year), high prices are legitimate here.
- Calibration, not a new rule: cheap replica sports jerseys (~NPR 600–700) are the normal local
  market — a low jersey price alone is not a counterfeit signal.
